items.label: section_header
items.text: KEY POINT

items.label: text
items.text: When we looked at the reaction between Mg and CuO above, we also wrote ions in the equation but we did not separate them completely because the ions are in a solid. We only separate everything like this when things are in solution. In a solution the ions are free to move around separately, in a solid they are not.

items.label: section_header
items.text: KEY POINT

items.label: text
items.text: Which copper(ll) salt you started with would not matter, as long as it was soluble in water. Copper(ll) chloride or copper(ll) nitrate would react in exactly the same way with zinc because the chloride ions or the nitrate ions would again be spectator ions, not participating in the reaction.

items.label: text
items.text: The oxide ion (O²-) does not change in this reaction. It ends up with a different partner, but is totally unchanged itself.

items.label: text
items.text: What is happening in this reaction is that magnesium atoms are turning into magnesium ions. The magnesium atoms lose electrons to form magnesium ionn          a e  awe have described this as a redox reaction above in terms of loss/gain of oxygen, but now we can see that it was not the oxygen that was actually the important part, it has not changed! To understand what is happening better, we need a more fundamental definition of oxidation and reduction:

items.label: list_item
items.text: oxidation is loss of electrons

items.label: list_item
items.text: reduction is gain of electrons.

items.text: DISPLACEMENT REACTIONS INVOLVING SOLUTIONS OF SALTS

items.label: text
items.text: Salts are compounds such as copper(ll) sulfate, silver nitrate or sodium chloride. You will find a definition of what a salt is on page 173. This section explores some reactions between metals and solutions of salts in water.

items.label: text
items.text: The copper is displaced by the more reactive zinc. The blue colour of the copper(ll) sulfate solution fades as colourless zinc sulfate solution is formed:

items.label: formula
items.text: Z n ( s ) + C u S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) \rightarrow Z n S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) + C u ( s )

items.label: text
items.text: The zinc and the copper are metals consisting simply of atoms, but the copper(ll) sulfate and the zinc sulfate are metal compounds and so are ionic.

items.label: text
items.text: The equation can be rewritten showing the ions:

items.label: text
items.text: We can see that the sulfate ions are exactly the same on both sides of the equation - they have not changed at all in the reaction. We call the sulfate ions here spectator ions. Removing the spectator ions (because they aren't changed during the reaction) leaves:

items.label: formula
items.text: Z n ( s ) + C u ^ { 2 + ( a q ) } \rightarrow Z n ^ { 2 + ( a q ) } + C u ( s )

items.label: text
items.text: This is called an ionic equation and just shows the things that change in the reaction.
